final.title: She Leans Toward Her Own
final.source_seed: The mother of the devoted: She turns toward the viewer, recognising them as Her own.
final.logline: Tara's gaze settles on you and She leans gently closer, and the star above Her crown brightens in answer.
final.hook: In the first 1.5 seconds Her calm open eyes settle on the lens and Her head and shoulders begin a slow, small lean toward you, so Her face grows slightly closer.
final.story: Devotees at Tarapith call Tara a mother to those who call on Her, though She is also a fierce protector. One devotional account tells of the saint Bamakhepa, who was beaten for eating the offering first. Tara is said to have appeared in a queen's dream and told her to feed him first because he was Her son. This is a devotional story, and the clip does not retell it literally. It carries the feeling of the fierce one turning toward someone and recognising them as Her own. She meets the viewer's eyes with a calm, soft face and leans a few degrees closer, and the star above Her crown, already in the reference portrait, brightens gently in answer. That brightening is a creators' symbol for being noticed, not a textual detail. The third eye stays unlit throughout, as in the reference. The tiger-skin wrap and skull garland stay in view. The loose hair in the reference differs from the matted or braided hair of the tradition. This is logged for human review, and the framing keeps attention on the face and the star.
final.loop: The clip ends on the held, closer gaze with the star bright. The editor loops it with a short crossfade back to the opening portrait, so the replay reads as Her turning toward you again and the render does not need to reverse its motion.
final.share_trigger: Sent to someone going through a hard time. The moment Tara looks straight at you, leans in and the star above Her brightens reads as being seen and cared for, and it promises nothing more.
final.caption_hook: Send this to someone who needs to be seen.
final.audio: A low, steady tone under faint, quiet water, with one soft low bell note and a gentle breath as the star brightens, then fading into the tone.

concept.title: Stern, Then Soft
concept.source_seed: Fierce protector, tender mother: the Ugra gaze that guards you softens for the one who calls (the 'feed him first, he is my son' story).
concept.logline: Her stern guarding stare melts into a tender smile, and Her third eye lights softly as the viewer is welcomed in.
concept.hook: At 0.3s Her brows lower and Her jaw firms into a stern, guarding stare straight at the viewer.
concept.story: She is a fierce protector who turns tender toward her own. The stern stare shows the guardian standing between the viewer and the dark. The softening shows the mother who feeds her devoted son first. The third eye lighting is the visible sign that the viewer has been recognised. No invented symbols; the light is a simple reading of the third eye.
concept.loop: The smile relaxes to the calm opening expression while the third eye glow settles to a faint gleam. The last frame echoes the first calm portrait, so the stern look at the start reads as a new beginning.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to a friend in a hard season, or to a mother, with the message 'she's tough on what hurts you and gentle with you.' The contrast is understood instantly.
concept.caption_hook: She guards you like a storm. She holds you like a mother.
concept.audio: A low, soft drone with one distant bell as the smile forms. Quiet night-water ambience underneath.

concept.title: Found You
concept.source_seed: The mother of the devoted: She turns toward the viewer, recognising them as Her own.
concept.logline: Her gaze searches the dark water, then finds the viewer and warms, and the guiding star above Her crown brightens.
concept.hook: At 0.5s Her eyes leave the viewer and Her head begins a slow turn to the side, as if She is searching the water.

concept.loop: After the star brightens, Her gaze holds steady and level on the viewer, as in the first frame. A replay makes the viewer feel looked for again.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone who feels unseen or far from home, with the message 'she's looking for you.' The direct-gaze moment is personal and easy to forward.

concept.title: Before the Voyage
concept.source_seed: Before the voyage: the goddess the seafarer prays to before crossing; she looks out over the dark water and clears the way.
concept.logline: She turns Her gaze to the dark horizon, the guiding star above Her blazes brighter, and She looks back to the viewer.
concept.hook: At 0.5s Her head begins a slow, restrained turn toward the distant black horizon.
concept.story: Traders of the old coast prayed to her before they crossed the sea. Here She does what they hoped for. She looks out over the dark water, her star brightens to mark the way, and She turns back to the traveller. The star acting as a signal is an invented symbol, a simple visual reading of her name meaning 'star'.
concept.loop: She turns back to face the viewer in the opening pose, and the star settles to its original glow. The clip ends on the first frame, so it loops cleanly.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone starting a trip, a move or a new chapter, with the message 'she's clearing the way for you.' It is a travel blessing in 10 seconds.
concept.caption_hook: Before you cross anything new, let Her look at the dark first.
concept.audio: Slow, low ambient pads with a faint, distant ship's bell. A soft rising swell as the star brightens.

shots.camera: Eye level, locked, with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her head turns slowly to the left and Her eyes lift to the black horizon, and the bright star above Her crown grows steadily brighter, as if lighting the far way. Her hair settles slowly.
shots.purpose: Gives a clear action with a clear consequence. The guardian looks ahead on the viewer's behalf.

shots.camera: Slow push-in at eye level, keeping the crown centered with clear space above the star.
shots.action: Her head turns back to face the viewer and Her eyes settle on them with a calm nod of the chin, so the star above Her crown softens back to its original glow, as if the way is clear.
shots.purpose: Closes the journey and returns to the opening frame for a clean loop.

virality: The star brightening is the one consequence, and the text admits it is an invented symbol. It also carries a lot of the story with little visible action.

virality: A nod of the chin and a star returning to its original glow is a subtle ending with no payoff, and it undoes the brightening, which weakens the climax.

concept.title: The Stride
concept.source_seed: The advancing stride: She steps toward you through the water with the unstoppable force the verses describe.
concept.logline: Tara steps once toward the viewer through the dark water, and rings of ripples spread out behind Her stride.
concept.hook: At 0.5s Her eyes harden, Her weight shifts forward and one foot starts to lift from the shallow water.
concept.story: The texts describe Her advancing with unstoppable force. Here that force is restrained to one slow, certain step. The ripples are the visible proof that She is coming for you. No invented symbols.
concept.loop: The step lands and She settles back into the calm opening stance. The rings fade toward stillness, so the end rhymes with the calm first frame.
concept.share_trigger: Sent as a 'help is on the way' message to someone facing something big. Also a strong pick for people who like powerful, cinematic goddess clips.
concept.caption_hook: When everything feels too heavy, She walks toward it, not away.
concept.audio: A slow, deep drum pulse at a walking pace, one beat on the footfall. A cold wind-free hush behind it.

shots.camera: Eye level, locked on the opening framing, with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her gaze hardens and Her weight shifts forward, and Her foot lifts slowly from the water, so a few small drops fall from Her toes. The serpent armbands catch a cold gleam.
shots.purpose: Shows intent and force right away. The shift of weight is a body action the model handles reliably.

shots.camera: Slow, steady glide backward at eye level, keeping Her at the same size with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her foot lowers into the shallow water in one slow step, and soft rings of ripples spread outward across the dark surface. Her hair sways slightly and settles.
shots.purpose: Delivers the payoff. One step has one clear visible consequence (the rings), and it conveys advancing protection.

feedback: virality: This is the only concept in which the goddess visibly DOES something with a visible consequence: a step, ripples, and drops of water. It meets the 'must DO something' rule.
virality: The stride and the ripple rings are physical, easy to understand and easy to render. It also ties to the pratyalidha iconography from the sources.
virality: The hook (foot lifting, weight shifting) starts at 0.5s and is readable, but 'one foot lifts' is a slow-motion build. It needs to be punchy in the first 1.5s.
virality: A backward camera glide with a figure stepping forward can cause scale and perspective drift in a video model. The foot must also land believably in shallow water.
virality: Standing over a corpse is omitted, which is wise, but the 'help is on the way' message depends on the stride reading as protective, not threatening.
virality: Loop is workable (step lands, she settles) but the return to the 'calm opening stance' is a slight reset rather than a seamless loop.
virality: Novelty is higher than the face-only concepts, since most AI devotional clips show a standing figure.
authenticity: Strongly grounded in the pratyalidha stride from the Nila Tantra and Tantrasara verses (secondary summaries). It is the most iconographically faithful concept.

authenticity: The verse stride is over a corpse (often Shiva) with a terrifying laugh and weapons. Reducing it to a gentle wade with ripples omits that context. This is acceptable and arguably sensible for reverence, but the concept should not claim to depict the verses fully.

authenticity: 'Help is on the way' and the caption 'She walks toward it, not away' read as modern self-help framing. They are plausible for a protective goddess, but the sources do not describe her as a rescuer arriving on cue.
authenticity: Eyes 'harden' could tip toward menace or action-movie tone if rendered carelessly.
authenticity: The viewer is placed as the one being approached, with no framing that the force is protective rather than threatening.

feasibility: A full-body step is a large pose change and the riskiest motion in the brief. A lifted foot, a weight shift, drops falling from the toes and expanding ripple rings stack several moving elements.
feasibility: Water and fluid physics are on the avoid list: ripples, drops and surface reflections regenerate independently and tend to break.
feasibility: The 'slow glide backward' camera must match Her forward step so She stays the same size. That is a compound camera-and-subject motion and invites scale drift.
feasibility: Her feet and the water may not be in frame 1 or the reference portrait; a waist-up portrait would not show a lifted foot at all. The foot and toes would be invented content.
feasibility: The serpent armband 'cold gleam' is a further small glow, and the hair sway is a fifth moving element.
feasibility: The ripples are specified as 'rings spreading outward', which means sequential, timed effects.
virality fix: Cut the build: start with the foot already mid-lift at frame 1, and land the step at about 3-4s so the ripples carry the rest.
virality fix: Ripples should be big and clear, and the drum beat should hit exactly on the footfall.
virality fix: Add a second cheap consequence, such as the dark water brightening or parting along the ripple rings, only if it does not add complexity.
virality fix: Fix the framing so the full legs and water are visible, since the ripples are the payoff and need to be in frame.
virality fix: Add a protective cue (a steady, calm face with open eyes toward the viewer) so the stride does not read as menacing.
authenticity fix: Make the story note explicit that the stride is a restrained reading of pratyalidha, with the corpse, laugh and weapons deliberately left out for reverence.
authenticity fix: Have the gaze read as resolute and compassionate rather than hard, and avoid any aggressive or predatory feel.
authenticity fix: Revise the caption to something like 'The fierce one steps toward your fear, not away from you.'
authenticity fix: Do not add any corpse or Shiva imagery to compensate.
feasibility fix: If the stride is kept, reduce it to a slow camera push-in with a slight forward lean of the upper body, and skip the footfall and ripples.
feasibility fix: Drop the water drops, the armband gleam and the glide-back camera.
feasibility fix: Check whether the reference framing shows her feet. If it does not, do not describe them.
feasibility fix: Alternatively convert it to a 'slow step forward' like the Kali render that worked, with a single push-in and no water interaction.

concept.title: The Look of a Mother
concept.source_seed: The mother of the devoted: She turns toward the viewer, recognising them as Her own.
concept.logline: Her head inclines and Her gaze settles on the viewer with a softening expression, and Her third eye brightens gently, as if recognising a child.
concept.hook: From the first frame Her eyes are open and Her head begins a slow incline toward the viewer, while the camera eases in and Her gaze settles on you.
concept.story: In the Tarapith tradition She is the fierce protector who is also a mother. In the story of the devoted Bamakhepa, She tells a queen to feed him first because he is Her son. This clip shows that moment of recognition. Her calm face softens, Her head inclines, Her eyes meet the viewer, and Her third eye brightens softly in answer. The soft brightening of the third eye is an invented symbol of recognition, not a textual detail. Tarapith is also where tradition says Sati's third eye (some sources say eyeball) fell, and Her name means star and also the pupil of the eye. The third eye is already in the opening frame and only brightens. It does not snap open as a sudden power.
concept.loop: In the last second Her head returns level, Her expression settles back to calm, and the third eye dims to its unlit state. The final frame matches the opening portrait, so the clip restarts as if She has looked at you again.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone who is going through a hard time, with 'she looks at you like a mother.' It is a gentle, comforting gaze that is easy to share without explanation.
concept.caption_hook: Tara means star, and the pupil of the eye.
concept.audio: Faint, quiet water at the start, with a soft low tone that warms and swells as Her gaze meets the viewer, then fades gently with the glow.

shots.camera: Slow push-in at eye level from the starting portrait framing, crown centered and fully framed with the star above it.
shots.action: Her head inclines a few degrees toward the viewer and Her gaze settles directly on the lens. Her calm expression softens into a gentle, warm look, which makes the third eye on Her forehead begin to glow faintly. Her hair settles slowly under gravity.
shots.purpose: Motion starts in the first second. The viewer feels Her attention turn to them, and the soft glow ties the expression change to the third eye.

shots.camera: Continued slow push-in at eye level, crown centered and fully framed with clear space around the star.
shots.action: She holds the warm, steady gaze and the third eye brightens to a soft silver-blue, which lightly lights Her brow and the base of the crown. In the final second Her head returns level and Her expression settles back to calm, so the third eye dims to its unlit state.
shots.purpose: This is the payoff, the moment of recognition. One gentle brightening answers Her gaze, and the return to the opening pose makes the loop rhyme.

feedback: virality: Weak hook: a head tilt of 'a few degrees' plus a slow push-in is barely visible motion on a phone. It reads as a near-static portrait, which is the 'goddess stands there' pattern the rubric penalises.

virality: The goddess does almost nothing. An incline and a softer expression have no consequence in the world: no water, object or other visible change. The only consequence is a faint glow, and glow-only scenes are penalised.

virality: The payoff is too subtle. Warm gaze to faint third-eye glow to return is hard to read in a 10s clip, and a micro-expression shift from calm to 'warm' will probably not render reliably in a video model.
virality: The hold is weak. There is no question or surprise, so viewers know within 2 seconds that nothing else will happen, and completion suffers.

virality: The loop is mechanically perfect (end frame equals opening frame), but the return to calm in the last second undoes the emotional payoff. The viewer gets 'she looked, then she un-looked', which feels like an animation reset rather than a satisfying loop.
virality: The 'star' and 'pupil of the eye' wordplay lives only in the caption. Nothing on screen shows a star responding, so the clever idea is not visualised. The caption is trivia, not a hook.
virality: The shot is calm and sleepy for a fierce tantric goddess. It is generic AI-devotional-clip territory, with low novelty and a low save value.

authenticity: The Bamakhepa story is a devotional anecdote from Tarapith, and this concept leans on it for the 'mother' reading without saying so. The story field does name it as tradition, but it is not framed as a devotional account, and nothing in the visuals ties the clip to it.

authenticity: The third-eye brightening is flagged as an invented symbol, which is honest. But the story then ties it to the Tarapith eye legend and the 'pupil of the eye' meaning, which makes an invention look textually grounded. 'Tara' meaning pupil is a real but secondary sense, and the Tarapith legend says the eye fell. It does not say the eye glows in recognition.

authenticity: The dossier's Tarapith account is 'third eye (some say eyeball)'. The concept uses 'third eye' for the legend without repeating the variance in the caption or the story logic. The caption_hook 'Tara means star, and the pupil of the eye' is accurate but gives no context for a general viewer and may look like a pun.

authenticity: The pure soft gaze presents only the tender, maternal side. The dossier's iconography is wrathful (corpse, pratyalidha, terrifying laugh). Without any trace of the Ugra aspect, a devotee could find it a generic benevolent-goddess portrait. This is acceptable as one aspect, but the loop contains nothing of Tara's power or crossing-over purpose.

authenticity: The anchor's loose hair departs from the dossier's matted or braided jata. 'Her hair settles slowly under gravity' draws attention to the loose hair instead of correcting or avoiding it.

authenticity: The share trigger, 'she looks at you like a mother', makes a personal claim about the goddess's relationship to the viewer. It is gentle and consistent with the tradition's mother-child devotion, but it should not promise outcomes or blessings.
feasibility: Mostly plays to Seedance's strengths: a face-centred shot, a slow push-in, a small head incline, a gaze settling and a faint expression change. It is the safer of the two concepts.

feasibility: The brief's mandatory-clip logic is sound, but the actions are the same two beats as the loop and the shot split: 'incline, glow, return level, dim'. That is four sequential state changes (incline, expression soften, third eye brighten, then reverse everything). The reversal in the last second is a second-by-second timing dependency the model cannot be told to hit. Seedance usually drifts rather than returning exactly to the start pose.

feasibility: The third eye glow is a dense-glow effect on a small facial region. It risks flicker and shimmer, and it may bleed into skin tone or change the eye's shape. The 'brightens to soft silver-blue' colour change is a second change on top of the glow itself, and the dim back to 'unlit state' adds another.

feasibility: 'Third eye already in the opening frame' is asserted, but the dossier notes the anchor's third eye exists without saying it is a visibly unlit state. If the reference portrait shows the third eye at some other state, the 'dims to unlit state' loop target is unreliable.
feasibility: The loop claim that the final frame 'matches the opening portrait' cannot be guaranteed in a single continuous render. Treat it as a hope, not a design.

feasibility: Lit brow and 'the base of the crown' lit by the glow adds a lighting change on a second area, and the star above the crown is not asked to do anything, which is fine, but 'clear space around the star' adds framing demands during a push-in that may crop the crown.

feasibility: Hair 'settles under gravity' is fine, but combined with the head incline, expression change, glow and push-in it brings the moving elements to about four, above the limit of two besides settling hair.

virality fix: Put a bigger, unmistakable physical action in the first 1.5s, for example her eyes snapping to the lens and the water around her visibly shivering or stilling, or the star above the crown flaring when her eyes land on you.
virality fix: Give the gaze a visible consequence. When she looks at you, the dark water goes glass-still, or ripples reaching the lens calm. One simple cause-and-effect beats a mood shift.
virality fix: Show the pupil/star pun on screen: the third eye lights and the star above brightens in sync, or a reflection of the star appears in her eye. That gives the caption a visual payoff.

virality fix: Make the loop the payoff, not a reset. End on a still, softened gaze that cuts back to the opening look, or have the glow fade into the opening glow, instead of walking the expression back.
virality fix: Cut the 4s+6s structure to one continuous move so the emotional turn lands by about 5s and the rest is held.
virality fix: If keeping the concept, add a send hook such as on-screen text 'Who needs to hear this?' rather than relying on a quiet face change.
authenticity fix: Name the Bamakhepa story in the caption or on-screen text as 'a Tarapith devotional story', not as established doctrine.

authenticity fix: Separate the invented glow from the tradition. Keep the symbol, but do not tie it in the story text to the Tarapith eye legend as if it were the same thing. Give the star/pupil etymology its own caption line, and mention 'some say eyeball' if the Tarapith legend is cited.

authenticity fix: Keep the calm opening portrait's hint of the fierce aspect, such as steady eyes or the tiger-skin and skull garland staying visible, so the softening reads as the Ugra mother and not a generic kind goddess.
authenticity fix: Frame or compose so that the hair does not become a focal motion detail. Avoid noting it as a feature, and keep the jata departure on the human review list.
authenticity fix: Keep any caption or comment copy free of promises, such as 'she will answer you'. Phrase it as 'devotees say' or 'in the Tarapith tradition'.
feasibility fix: Drop the return-to-level and dim-to-unlit ending. End on the warm gaze with the glow held steady, and let the loop rely on the cut-back to the start rather than a rendered reversal.
feasibility fix: Cut it to two moving elements: the slow push-in plus one facial change. Choose either the head incline plus softening gaze, or the third-eye glow, not both.

feasibility fix: If the glow stays, make it very faint and warm-toned, with no colour shift and no lighting spill onto the brow or crown. Phrase it as 'the third eye gently lights', one change in one direction.
feasibility fix: Remove the crown framing constraints and just say 'waist-up, crown and star stay in frame', or push in less so nothing crops.
feasibility fix: Confirm in the prompt that the third eye is closed or unlit in the reference portrait before claiming it dims or brightens.

concept.title: She Steps Toward You
concept.source_seed: Fierce protector, tender mother: the Ugra gaze that guards you softens for the one who calls (the 'feed him first, he is my son' story).
concept.logline: She steps forward through the dark water with a steady gaze, then softens into a gentle smile as Her third eye brightens.
concept.hook: From the first second She takes a slow step toward the viewer with a steady, serious gaze, and wide ripples spread across the dark water around Her.
concept.story: Her fierce protection and Her tenderness are one compassion, not two faces. The advancing step is the guardian coming straight to the one who calls. The softening smile is the mother who feeds her devoted son first, from the devotional story told at Tarapith. The third eye brightening softly is a cinematic touch and not a meaning taken from the tradition. The silver-blue tone is a stylistic choice.
concept.loop: The clip ends on a calm, soft expression close to the opening calm portrait, with the water settling after Her step. Replaying starts again on the calm portrait and the step, so the arc reads as She arrives, then comforts.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to a friend in a hard season, or to a mother, with the message 'she comes straight toward what you're carrying, and she's gentle with you.'
concept.caption_hook: She protects you fiercely. She holds you like a mother.
concept.audio: A low steady drone with the slow sound of one step in water, then one distant soft bell as the smile forms. Quiet night-water ambience underneath.

shots.camera: Eye level, slow steady push-in from the opening framing, with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: She takes one slow step toward the viewer with a firm, steady gaze, and the dark water around Her ripples outward in wide, gentle rings. Her hair settles slowly as She moves.
shots.purpose: Gives a clear, readable action in the first second. The step shows the protector coming toward the viewer, and the ripples show the effect on the world.

shots.camera: Same eye-level push-in, easing to almost still, with the crown centered and clear space above the star.
shots.action: She stops, Her brows release and a faint, tender smile forms, so the ripples fade into calm water and Her third eye brightens with a soft silver-blue light across Her forehead.
shots.purpose: Delivers the payoff. The arriving guardian turns into the tender mother, and the water settling shows the change in the world.

feedback: virality: The hook is much stronger. A step toward the viewer with ripples radiating is specific, visible motion from frame 1, and it matches the pratyalidha iconography and a real seed.
virality: The ripples give her action a visible consequence in the world, which is exactly what the rubric asks for, and the 'fierce then tender' arc is a real mini-story with a payoff.

virality: Rendering risk: a standing figure taking a believable step through water while the camera pushes in is doable, but 'one slow step' plus wide ripples can look floaty. Her smile forming as the brows release is a subtle facial change that models often botch, and it risks looking uncanny on a fierce blue goddess.

virality: The loop is soft. It ends on a smiling or tender expression 'close to' the opening calm portrait, but the opening is a stern step, not a calm portrait. The cut back from a smile to a mid-step is not seamless.

virality: The third-eye brightening is again an invented glow stacked on top of the smile and the water settling. That is three simultaneous payoff changes (smile, ripples fading, glow), which dilutes the single clear moment.
virality: The step slows into near-still for the second half. Momentum drops after 5s, and the second shot risks being a static portrait with a glow.

virality: The caption and share trigger are good ('protects you fiercely, holds you like a mother'), but the fierce-to-tender turn is told by a barely visible smile, so the viewer may not feel it without the caption.

authenticity: The advancing step comes from the pratyalidha stance in the Nila Tantra verses, but the dossier describes that stance as an archer's stride over a corpse with a terrifying laugh. The concept turns it into a gentle walk through water and then a 'tender smile'. Ending on a smile moves away from the iconography. Tara's tantric imagery is a fierce, wrathful smile or laugh. A sweet smile risks reading as a generic benign goddess and may feel like trivialising to some devotees.

authenticity: The story merges two things the dossier keeps apart: the Ugra Tara aspect (relieves severe suffering) and the Bamakhepa 'feed him first' story. The Bamakhepa story has no stepping or advancing. Joining them as 'one compassion, not two faces' is a theological claim the research does not support. It is an interpretation presented as the story's meaning.

authenticity: The 'fierce to tender' arc implies that fierceness is the gate and tenderness is the resolution. In tantric understanding, her fierce form is itself the compassion. The arc risks a 'scary then nice' framing.

authenticity: Steps toward the viewer across water leaves the viewer in an ambiguous position: threatened, or saved? 'Guardian coming straight to the one who calls' is a devotional claim, and the concept does not clearly mark it as the creators' reading.

authenticity: Third-eye brightening and silver-blue are acknowledged as invented, which is good. But the concept also turns the hook's 'steady, serious gaze' into a stiff beat and does not say what the audience should understand it to mean.

authenticity: The share trigger, 'she comes straight toward what you're carrying, and she's gentle with you', makes the goddess's behaviour toward the viewer a promise. It is also close to commercial self-help messaging.
authenticity: Loose hair is again used as motion ('Her hair settles slowly as She moves') and highlights the departure from jata or Ekajata.

feasibility: The main action is a full-body step forward through water, which the brief warns against: water and fluids, large motion and physics. Ripples spreading in 'wide gentle rings' then 'fading into calm' is exactly the 'calming liquid' failure the guide lists, because reflections and the ripple physics regenerate independently.

feasibility: Too many moving elements: step, camera push-in, ripples, hair, then a face change (brows release, smile forms), then a third-eye glow, then ripples fading. That is well over the limit of two besides hair.

feasibility: Ripples that appear in the first second are not in the reference portrait, which has her standing in shallow dark water that is presumably still. Ripple appearance is an effect with no clear cause visible in frame 1 apart from the step.

feasibility: The concept relies on sequencing: 'step, then stop, then smile, then glow, then ripples fade'. Seedance renders one continuous clip and cannot be trusted to hit a 5-second handover, so the two-shot structure is fiction.

feasibility: A step forward is listed as reliable, but combined with a camera push-in the subject-to-camera distance changes twice over, so the crown framing 'centred and fully framed' will drift, and a walk forward with a pushing camera risks scale and identity drift.
feasibility: The expression arc (stern gaze to tender smile) is a large facial change, and a smile on a fierce, three-eyed face risks distorting the face or the third eye.
feasibility: The loop claim is weak: the ending 'close to the opening calm portrait' while the clip begins with a stern gaze means the opening frame and the final frame do not match.
feasibility: Audio mentions a step in water and a bell, which is fine, but irrelevant to render feasibility.

virality fix: Keep the step as the hook but make it decisive. Her stride should lunge or arrive close to the lens so the ripple hits the camera, giving a visceral 'she's coming for you' beat in the first 1.5s.

concept.title: She Leans Toward You
concept.source_seed: Fierce protector, tender mother: the guarding gaze softens for the one who calls (the 'feed him first, he is my son' story).
concept.logline: Tara leans slowly toward the viewer with a steady gaze, Her third eye lighting softly, then settles back upright into calm.
concept.hook: From the first second She leans slowly toward the viewer with a steady, serious gaze, Her face growing larger in the frame while the dark water stays still around Her.
concept.story: Her name is read as the one who carries across, and Her fierce three-eyed gaze is the gaze of a protector. The slow lean is a reach toward the viewer, as if to carry them across. The unsmiling face stays fierce throughout. The only change in Her look is a soft light in the third eye, which is the creators' cinematic touch. The silver-blue tone is also a stylistic choice. Devotees of Bamakhepa tell that She called him her son and had him fed first. Linking that devotional story to the protector's gaze is the creators' reading, not a claim from the texts. Her hair stays loose as in the reference image, which differs from the matted or braided hair of the tradition. That mismatch is flagged for human review.
concept.loop: The clip begins and ends on the same calm, upright portrait with the third eye unlit and the water still. On replay the lean begins again, so the loop reads as She turns toward you once more.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone going through a hard stretch, as a quiet image of being watched over. It is shared with the line that devotees in the Bengal tradition call Her mother.
concept.caption_hook: In the devotional story, the fierce goddess calls her devotee her son.
concept.audio: A low steady drone with quiet night-water ambience. One soft, distant bell sounds as the third eye lights and fades as She settles back.

shots.camera: Eye level, locked frame matching the opening portrait, with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: She leans slowly forward from the waist with a firm, steady gaze fixed on the viewer, which brings Her face closer and larger in the frame, and Her third eye lights softly with a silver-blue glow as She leans. Her hair settles gently under its own weight.
shots.purpose: Opens with a clear, readable action from the first second. The lean is a reach toward the viewer, and the lit third eye marks the moment Her attention rests on them.

shots.camera: Same eye-level locked frame, crown centered and fully framed, with clear space above the star.
shots.action: She holds the steady gaze for a breath, then eases back upright to the starting pose, which returns Her face to its original size in the frame, and the third eye glow fades back to unlit as She settles.
shots.purpose: Delivers the payoff and a seamless loop. The fierce gaze stays unbroken, the leaning-in resolves into calm, and the final frame matches the opening portrait.

feedback: virality: The lean is a simple, readable motion that the model can render, and the return to upright gives a real loop. This is the better-built clip of the two.

virality: The hook is still a slow lean from a calm portrait. Visible motion starts at once, but 'slowly' and 'steady' mean there is no punch, and a lean from the waist on a three-quarter portrait risks looking like a zoom or a stiff tilt.

virality: The payoff is thin. A third eye lighting and fading is a glow-only beat, and the clip's own text calls it a cinematic touch with no textual basis. Nothing consequential happens in the world around her, and the water stays still, so the gesture has no consequence.
virality: The lean-in then lean-back structure reads as a breathing animation. Viewers get no question to hold them for 10s, so completion relies on the loop alone.

virality: Send-worthiness is moderate. 'Being watched over' is a real emotion, but the image alone does not say 'mother'. The fierce unsmiling face plus a lean can read as menacing, which undercuts the comfort the caption promises.

virality: Saves are low, as there is no information or surprise to keep. The one distinctive idea (fierce gaze that does not soften) fights the 'tender mother' seed and leaves the story seed barely visible.
virality: Silver-blue glow and the bell are generic devotional ambience, and novelty is low.

authenticity: The caption asserts the story ('the fierce goddess calls her devotee her son') without naming Bamakhepa or Tarapith, and the story field concedes that linking it to the gaze is the creators' reading. A viewer gets a free-floating claim.

authenticity: Leaning forward from the waist and then retreating reads as a jump-scare or a peer-in move. Tara's iconography is hieratic and grounded, not a creature leaning at the viewer. A devotee could find it faintly menacing or trivialising, and the third-eye bell cue pushes it toward a horror beat.

authenticity: The silver-blue third-eye glow is an invention, and the tradition's own third-eye story (Sati's eye at Tarapith) is not used. The story field says 'creators' cinematic touch', which is honest but gives nothing the dossier supports.
authenticity: The 'carries across' reading of the lean is a stretch. Nothing in the frame (no water crossing, no path) shows ferrying or rescue, which the dossier calls her core story.
authenticity: There is no mention that the tiger-skin wrap or skull garland stay in frame, and the hair mismatch is left unresolved.

feasibility: A lean forward from the waist is a larger pose change than the model prefers. A restrained lean toward the camera is listed as reliable, but 'from the waist' on a three-quarter-length figure with a crown, skull garland and wrap risks body deformation and identity drift.

feasibility: The audio bell cue depends on the moment the eye lights, which cannot be controlled by timing.
feasibility: The statement that the water stays still is hard to guarantee while a figure in water moves, and water is a risky element.

concept.title: She Steps Toward Her Own
concept.source_seed: The mother of the devoted: She turns toward the viewer, recognising them as Her own.
concept.logline: Tara steps slowly toward the viewer, and the star above Her crown and Her third eye brighten together as Her gaze meets yours.
concept.hook: From the first frame Her open eyes are fixed on the lens and She takes one slow, firm step forward through the shallow water, so Her figure visibly grows nearer.
concept.story: In the Tarapith devotional tradition, Tara is the fierce protector who is also a mother. One devotional account tells of the saint Bamakhepa, who was beaten for eating the offering first. Tara is said to have appeared in a queen's dream and told her to feed him first because he was Her son. This is a devotional story, not established doctrine. The clip draws on that mother-and-child feeling and does not retell the story literally. Her unwavering gaze and steady stride show the protective strength, and the tiger-skin wrap and skull garland stay in view. When She stops, the star above Her crown and Her third eye brighten together, softly and in one warm tone. This pairing is an invented symbol of recognition. It is not a textual detail and does not come from the Tarapith eye legend. That legend says Sati's third eye (some say an eyeball) fell at Tarapith, and it says nothing of a glow. Separately, Her name means star and also the pupil of the eye, which the star and the eye answering together echo visually. Human review note: the anchor's loose hair departs from the matted or braided hair of the tradition, so the clip keeps hair as a minor detail.
concept.loop: The clip ends on Her nearer, steady gaze with the star and third eye still glowing. A cut back to the opening portrait shows Her calm and unlit again, as if She is waiting to step toward the next viewer. The loop relies on that restart and not on a rendered reversal.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone going through a hard time, with 'In the Tarapith tradition, Tara is called a mother to her devotees.' It offers comfort through the image and promises nothing. Viewers are invited in the caption to send it to someone who needs it.
concept.caption_hook: Devotees at Tarapith speak of Tara as a mother: the fierce one who steps toward her own. Her name means star, and also the pupil of the eye.
concept.audio: Faint, quiet water at the start. A low, soft tone rises under Her step and warms when She stops and the star and third eye brighten, then holds gently to the end.

shots.camera: Camera holds steady at eye level on the three-quarter-length portrait, crown centered and fully in frame with the star above it.
shots.action: She takes one slow, firm step toward the viewer with Her eyes fixed on the lens, which brings Her figure visibly closer and makes Her face and shoulders fill more of the frame. Her third eye stays unlit as in the reference portrait.
shots.purpose: A clear, readable action from the first second: the fierce protector advances. The growing closeness is the visible consequence and sets up the question of what happens when She arrives.

shots.camera: Camera holds steady at eye level, crown centered and fully in frame with the star above it.
shots.action: She comes to a stop and holds Her steady gaze on the viewer, and in answer the star above Her crown and Her third eye brighten together in one soft, warm tone, so Her face glows gently as the clip ends. Her hair settles under gravity as She stops.
shots.purpose: The payoff: recognition. Her arrival is met by the star and the third eye lighting together, which shows the star-and-pupil meaning on screen. The clip ends on the held glow without a reset.

feedback: virality: Hook is weak. A slow step toward the lens is just a slow push-in on a portrait. Nothing happens in the first 1.5s except gradual scaling, and the 'one slow, firm step' is easy for the model to render as a drifting zoom or a float, not a real step with water reaction.
virality: The payoff arrives at 5s. The first half is a plain approach with no change, so viewers have no reason to expect a payoff and many will swipe before the glow.

virality: Loop is broken by its own admission. It ends on a close, glowing Tara and 'cuts back' to a calm, unlit, farther portrait. That is a hard visual jump, not a flow into the opening frame, and the shot list even says 'without a reset', which contradicts the loop claim.

virality: The gesture has a consequence (glow) but the glow is a generic 'soft warm light' on a face and a star. This is the glow-only trope the rubric penalises, and it is invented symbolism that carries no instant meaning on a phone.
virality: Two lit elements (star above crown and third eye) in one tone is subtle at phone size. The star is far from the face, so the viewer's eye has to split.
virality: Send-worthiness is decent (comfort to someone struggling), but the 'mother who steps toward her own' idea relies on caption text to land. The image alone reads as 'goddess walks at camera'.
virality: Novelty is middling. Approaching-camera goddess with a glowing third eye is common in AI devotional clips. The Bamakhepa 'feed him first' link is almost invisible in the visuals.

virality: Keeping skull garland, tiger skin and crown fully in frame while she gets closer and her face fills more of the frame is contradictory framing, and invites model drift in the crown and star.

authenticity: The paired star and third-eye glow is the creators' own invention. The story field says so honestly, but the caption and on-screen text do not. A viewer will likely read the glow as canonical 'recognition', and a devotee could take it as a claim about Tara.

authenticity: The glow is soft, warm and affirming, which risks sanitising the Ugra aspect of the third eye. The dossier describes fierce, bright eyes and a terrifying laugh. One slow step is a gentle gloss on the pratyalidha stride, which advances with force.

authenticity: 'Recognising them as Her own' casts every viewer as a devotee. Tara calls her devotees her children, and the story is about one specific saint, Bamakhepa. The clip leans on that story without naming him or Tarapith on screen.

authenticity: The star-and-pupil meaning of the name is well grounded, but the star 'answering' the eye is a visual pun that is not part of the tradition. It needs to stay framed as a reading, not a fact.
authenticity: The loose hair departs from the jata or Ekajata braid. It is flagged, but the shot actions still call attention to the hair settling.
authenticity: The caption says 'fierce one who steps toward her own', but the on-screen step is calm and measured. The fierceness comes from the gaze alone.

feasibility: The 'one slow step forward' is a strength (the Kali render did it well), but this concept stacks three changes: the step, the star brightening and the third eye brightening. That is near the limit of 'one intentional change per clip'. The glow is dense light and could flicker or shimmer.

feasibility: Two shots with a second-by-second split (5 s walking, then 5 s stopping and glowing) rely on timing inside a continuous render. Seedance cannot be told to walk for exactly 5 s, stop, and only then light up. Expect the glow to start early or the step to run the whole clip.

feasibility: The camera is described as 'locked' while the figure steps forward in shallow water. Stepping through water risks ripples, splashes and reflections that regenerate independently, and these count as extra moving elements beyond the step and the glow.

feasibility: The star above the crown is a small, distant, glowing element that has to brighten on its own while the head moves toward the camera. Small tracked glowing objects are a known weak point and the star may drift or duplicate.

feasibility: A step toward the camera at three-quarter length changes scale (the figure grows), and this can shift the face and crown. The crown with the sun disc, skull garland and tiger-skin wrap all stay in frame and must hold identity through the scale change. 'Crown centered and fully in frame' is hard to keep while She advances.
feasibility: Hair settling under gravity on stopping is another timed event, though minor.
feasibility: The loop depends on a hard cut back to the portrait. The end state (glowing, nearer) differs from the start, so the loop is not seamless, though it is acceptable for a restart.
feasibility: The audio cues (tone rising under the step, warming at the glow) imply timing the video cannot guarantee.

virality fix: Make the step physical and instant: her foot lands in the first second and a ring of ripples spreads across the dark water, with the water visibly parting or lighting under her foot. Ripples give the model a legible consequence.

virality fix: Put the payoff earlier and make it a single clear change. For example, the third eye opens or ignites on the beat of the second step at about 3s, with a pronounced pulse, not a slow warm fade.

virality fix: Fix the loop. Make the final frame match the first: start on the close, glowing frame and end after she has stepped back or the glow has dimmed to the same state, or start at a tight close-up and end at the same crop. Do not rely on a hard cut between mismatched frames.
virality fix: Drop the star-above-crown glow or tie it to the eye with a visible light line, so there is one unmistakable event. One lit eye beats two lit elements.
virality fix: Give the viewer a stake in the first second: her eyes snap open on the lens as the first step lands, so the 'she noticed you' moment is the hook itself.
virality fix: Use a stronger recognition gesture at the end, such as her hand reaching toward the lens and stopping just short, so the 'my own' meaning is visible without the caption.
authenticity fix: Keep the 'invented symbol' disclaimer in the pinned caption or comment, for example 'the glow is our artistic touch, not a textual detail'. Do not let it read as scripture.

authenticity fix: Keep the brightening restrained, and do not let the third eye glow turn sweet or sentimental. Keep the steady, unsmiling gaze and keep the tiger-skin wrap and skull garland visible in both shots.
authenticity fix: Name Bamakhepa and Tarapith in the caption as a devotional story ('devotees tell...'), and soften 'steps toward her own' to something like 'devotees call her mother'.
authenticity fix: Reduce hair motion to near-nothing, or frame tighter so the hair mismatch is not noticeable.
authenticity fix: Make the step firm, with a grounded stride and no drifting or gliding, so it echoes the pratyalidha stance.

feasibility fix: Drop the star glow and keep only one light change, the third eye warming softly. Or keep a single gentle glow shared by the third eye only, and let the star stay as in the reference portrait.

feasibility fix: Remove the shot split and write one continuous 10 s action: 'She takes one slow step toward the camera, gaze fixed on the lens, third eye gently warming as She comes closer.' No separate stop beat.

feasibility fix: Reduce water interaction. Say the water around Her feet stays nearly still, or frame at waist-up so the feet and water are mostly out of frame, and describe the step as a slow lean-and-advance of the upper body.
feasibility fix: Use a slow camera push-in combined with a very small step, so the camera produces most of the closeness and the body moves less. This keeps identity stable.
feasibility fix: Keep the glow subtle and slow, described as 'a faint warm light' rather than a bright dual brightening, to avoid shimmer.
feasibility fix: Make the audio a single steady tone rather than cues tied to specific moments.

concept.title: The Gaze That Softens
concept.source_seed: Fierce protector, tender mother: the Ugra gaze that guards you softens for the one who calls (the 'feed him first, he is my son' story).
concept.logline: Tara's stern gaze softens as She tilts Her head toward the viewer, and the star above Her crown brightens in answer.
concept.hook: In the first second Her stern, wide-open eyes lock onto the viewer and Her head begins to lower and tilt, so Her face drifts a little closer as the guardian look starts to change.
concept.story: Tara is the fierce protector, three-eyed and stern, and devotees also call Her mother. At Tarapith, devotees of Bamakhepa tell that She called him Her son and had him fed first. The clip shows that turn in Her face. The stern guarding gaze holds, then the head lowers and tilts, the brows ease and the eyes grow tender. The star above Her crown brightens in answer. Her name means star, so the brightening star is the creators' symbol for Her reply to the one who calls. It is not a claim from the texts. The third eye stays unlit, so nothing is added to Her iconography. The tiger-skin wrap and skull garland stay in view in the lower frame. Her hair is loose in the reference image, unlike the matted or braided hair of the tradition. That mismatch is flagged for human review. Linking the Bamakhepa story to this gaze is the creators' reading of a devotional tale.
concept.loop: The clip ends on the softened, tilted gaze and the brighter star. On replay it hard-cuts back to the stern upright portrait, so the loop reads as the guardian softening for you again.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone going through a hard stretch, or to a person who needs to be reminded that a stern protector can also be a mother. The softening face says 'mother' without words, and the caption names where the story comes from.
concept.caption_hook: Devotees of Bamakhepa at Tarapith tell that Tara, the fierce one, called him her son.
concept.audio: One low steady drone with quiet night-water ambience. A soft sustained tone rises gently under the second half as Her expression eases. No timed accents.

shots.camera: Eye level, matching the opening portrait, with a very slow, small push-in. The crown with its sun disc and the star above it stay centered and fully framed with headroom to spare.
shots.action: Her stern gaze holds the viewer, then Her head lowers a little and tilts to one side, which brings Her face slightly closer to the camera. The tiger-skin wrap and skull garland stay in view in the lower frame, and Her hair settles under its own weight.
shots.purpose: The hook is a clear, readable face action from the first second. The lowering tilt turns the guardian's stare into an approach toward the viewer, and the small push-in carries the movement without a body lean.

shots.camera: Same eye-level frame and the same very slow push-in, with the crown and star still centered and fully framed.
shots.action: With Her head still tilted, Her brows ease and Her eyelids soften, which changes Her expression from stern guardian to tender mother, and the star above Her crown brightens in answer. The clip ends on this held, softened gaze.
shots.purpose: The payoff makes the story visible: the fierce gaze softens for the one who calls, and the star above Her responds. The ending holds still, so the render has no reversal to get wrong.

feedback: virality: Hook is weak. 'Eyes lock on, head lowers and tilts a little' is a small, slow face drift, and on a phone it will read as a near-static portrait. No visible consequence in the first 1.5s.

virality: The payoff is a subtle expression change (brows ease, eyelids soften). Video models render this unreliably, and viewers scrolling at speed may not see it at all. The 'stern to tender' beat is the whole video and it is the least legible part.
virality: The star 'brightens in answer' is a glow-only change. The brief penalises glow-only scenes, and it is the same dull-to-bright device as most generic AI devotional clips.
virality: The goddess does very little. Tilting the head and softening the eyes is a pose change, not an action with a consequence. Nothing in the world reacts except a star.

virality: Loop is a hard cut from a soft, tilted, bright-star ending back to a stern upright portrait. The viewer feels the jump, and the 'softening again' reading depends on a cut. The loop is imposed rather than flowing.
virality: The ending holds still on the payoff for the back half of the clip. With a 5s hold on a subtle expression, completion will sag.
virality: Send-worthiness is plausible ('stern protector is also a mother') but the visual carries too little to trigger a send without the caption. The story is explained entirely in text.
virality: Novelty is low. A portrait of a goddess with a brightening star is the generic AI devotional clip. The Bamakhepa link is invisible on screen.
virality: The sun disc, star, skull garland and tiger skin all need to stay framed. That is a lot to hold for a face-centred shot, and a push-in risks cropping the crown.

authenticity: The core idea holds up. A fierce protector who is also a mother, drawn from the Bamakhepa 'feed him first, he is my son' story, matches the dossier. It adds nothing to Her iconography: the third eye stays unlit, and the sun disc, tiger skin and skull garland are unchanged.

authenticity: The story text discloses the creators' reading of the star and the Bamakhepa link, but the caption hook does not. Viewers who only see the caption get the devotional tale with no marker that the star brightening is invented. The star symbolism rests on 'star' as one etymology. That is acceptable, but it should be labelled as interpretation on screen or in the caption.

authenticity: Shot 1 says 'Her hair settles under its own weight.' That draws attention to the loose hair, which the dossier flags as departing from the matted jata or Ekajata braid. Nothing in the video explains the mismatch.

authenticity: 'Tender mother' softened brows and eyes lean toward sentimental. Tara's iconography is wrathful (pratyalidha stance, terrifying laugh), and the softening is the creators' device, not a textual scene. The softening is reverent but leaves out that the fierce form stays fierce.
authenticity: The caption says Tara 'called him her son' as plain fact. The dossier says she 'reportedly' appeared in a queen's dream. The hedge should be in the caption as well as the story.
authenticity: The hard cut back to the stern portrait on loop is fine, but it implies her softening is reversible or conditional. A devotee could read that as Her affection switching on and off.

feasibility: Concept is mostly a face action (head lowers and tilts, brows ease, eyes soften), which suits the model. The head lowering and tilting while the camera pushes in is a small combined motion, but it is within what the guide lists as reliable.

feasibility: Count of changes: head lower+tilt, expression shift, star brightening, push-in, hair settling. That is about three moving elements plus hair, right at the limit. The star brightening is a glow effect and may shimmer or flicker; it is the riskiest element.

feasibility: The expression change from stern to tender is subtle and hard to render. Seedance may under-deliver (barely visible) or over-deliver (a smile and identity drift). Brows easing and eyelids softening are two or three micro-changes bundled into one.

feasibility: The prompt structure leans on timing: shot 1 is the tilt, shot 2 is the softening and star, with 'holds, then lowers'. This is a sequential beat with a hold-then-change order inside a single continuous render, which the rubric penalises. The two-shot, 5s/5s split is only a narrative description, not a cut, and the render cannot honour it.

feasibility: 'Fully framed with headroom to spare' for the crown and star, while the camera pushes in and the head lowers, is in tension. The push-in plus the lowering head may crop the star, which is needed for the payoff.

feasibility: The loop claim of a hard-cut back to the stern portrait is fine for editing but does nothing for the render. A soft stern-to-tender change is a weak first-second hook with little visible cause and effect: nothing visibly causes the star to brighten.

feasibility: The skull garland and tiger-skin in the lower frame are only in frame 1 if the reference portrait shows them. The dossier says the anchor matches, so this is probably fine, but confirm the reference is framed low enough to include them. The crown's sun disc and star are in the reference per the round 3 note.

concept.title: She Leans Toward Her Own
concept.source_seed: The mother of the devoted: She turns toward the viewer, recognising them as Her own.
concept.logline: Tara leans toward the viewer, Her third eye flaring once as Her gaze locks on you, then She settles back to calm.
concept.hook: Within the first 1.5 seconds Her calm eyes lock onto the lens, She leans in so Her face grows toward you, and a first spark of light kindles in Her third eye.
concept.story: Devotees at Tarapith call Tara a mother to those who call on Her, though She is also the fierce protector. One devotional account tells of the saint Bamakhepa, who was beaten for eating the offering first. Tara is said to have appeared in a queen's dream and told her to feed him first because he was Her son. This is a devotional story, not established doctrine, and the clip does not retell it literally. It draws on the feeling of the fierce one turning toward someone and claiming them. She leans in with a steady, unsmiling gaze, and Her third eye flares once in a sharp, restrained pulse. The tiger-skin wrap and skull garland stay in view. The flaring third eye is an invented symbol for being noticed. It is our artistic touch, not a textual detail, and it does not come from the Tarapith legend of Sati's eye, which mentions no light. Her name also means star and the pupil of the eye. That is a reading we offer, not a claim about the tradition. The star above Her crown stays exactly as in the reference portrait so the light has one clear focus. The loose hair departs from the matted or braided hair of the tradition, so the clip gives it no attention.
concept.loop: The clip is built as a loop. It opens on the calm portrait with the third eye unlit. She leans in and the eye flares. Then She slowly straightens and the light fades until the last frame matches the first: upright, centered, calm, third eye unlit. The restart flows from the end frame with no jump in framing or light.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone going through a hard time, with the line 'Devotees at Tarapith call Tara mother.' The moment She looks straight at you and leans in reads as being seen, and it promises nothing. The caption invites viewers to send it to someone who needs to feel noticed.
concept.caption_hook: Devotees at Tarapith tell of Bamakhepa, the saint Tara called her son, and they call her mother. (The glowing eye is our artistic touch, not a textual detail.)
concept.audio: A single low, steady tone under faint, quiet water, held evenly from start to end with no cues tied to specific moments.

concept.title: She Comes When You Call
concept.source_seed: Fierce protector, tender mother: the Ugra gaze that guards you softens for the one who calls (the 'feed him first, he is my son' story).

concept.story: Tara is the fierce protector, three-eyed and unflinching, and devotees also call Her mother. Devotees at Tarapith tell that She reportedly appeared in a queen's dream and said the saint Bamakhepa was Her son and should be fed first. One firm step brings Her closer and ripples carry the movement out to the viewer. The step is the creators' symbol for Her answer. It is not a scene from the texts, and linking this tale to the step is the creators' reading of a devotional story. Her third eye stays unlit, and the sun disc, star and ornaments are unchanged from the reference. The hair is loose in the reference image, unlike the matted or braided hair of the tradition. The framing leaves the hair unremarked, and the mismatch is flagged for human review.

The replay cut to the opening frame is near-identical in composition, so it reads as a soft reset. concept.caption_hook: Devotees at Tarapith tell that Tara appeared in a queen's dream and said Bamakhepa was Her son. The step toward you is our symbol, not a textual detail.
concept.audio: Low steady drone with quiet night-water ambience. One soft low water sound as Her foot meets the water in the first second, then a gentle sustained tone that fades as the ripples settle.

shots.action: Her gaze stays fixed on the viewer as She presses one foot forward into the shallow water, which sends a ring of ripples spreading from Her feet across the dark surface toward the camera.
